title: AI Automation in Miami, FL | 22 Signals
description: AI automation for Miami brokerages, freight firms, clinics and hotels: fewer manual hand-offs, faster bilingual replies, and a CRM that stays up to date.
h1: AI automation for Miami teams buried in manual work
intro: We build AI automation for established Miami businesses: tools that route leads, read documents, draft replies in English and Spanish, and keep your CRM and spreadsheets in sync. Brokerages, freight forwarders, clinics and hotel groups use it to cut the copy-and-paste work their staff do every day, with a person stepping in whenever judgment is needed.

sections.h: The problem: good staff doing robot work
p: Walk through the back office of a busy Miami company and you see the same thing. A leasing coordinator copies inquiries from the website, Zillow and WhatsApp into a CRM by hand. A freight forwarder in Doral retypes shipment details from PDFs into a quote sheet. A med spa receptionist answers the same twelve questions about pricing and downtime, half of them in Spanish, before lunch.

None of that needs a new hire. It needs the work to move between systems on its own, with AI handling the reading, sorting and first drafts. That is what AI automation Miami companies ask us for: fewer hand-offs, faster replies, and staff freed for the work that actually needs them.

sections.h: How it works: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we start with the one process that annoys your team most. A 15-minute call is usually enough to tell whether automation is the right fix.
Plan: we map the process step by step, note every system it touches, and agree what the automation will and will not do. Dates go in writing.
Build: we build, test on real examples from your inbox or files, and run the new flow alongside the old one until the results match.
Grow: once one flow is stable we add the next, and we watch error logs so problems are caught before your customers notice.

sections.h: Bilingual by design, with humans in the loop
p: In Miami, an automation that only works in English only works for part of your customers. We design every customer-facing flow to handle English, Spanish and the mix of both that people actually type. Portuguese can be added for Brazilian buyers where it matters.

Every step in our AI automation, Miami or elsewhere, has a clear hand-off rule. Anything that touches pricing, medical advice, legal terms or an unhappy customer goes to a person with the full history attached. Staff stay in charge; the system just does the sorting and drafting.

Automations move data between systems, so we treat access carefully. We use the least access each tool needs, keep logs of what was sent where, and avoid sending patient, investor or payment data to tools that are not approved for it.

Florida's Information Protection Act requires most businesses to notify affected people within 30 days of a breach, and the Florida Digital Bill of Rights adds rules for companies that sell sensitive data. Texting customers also brings consent rules under the Florida Telephone Solicitation Act. We build consent capture into the flow and leave the legal sign-off to your counsel.

faqs.q: What is the best first automation for a Miami real estate brokerage?
faqs.a: Lead capture and routing. Inquiries arrive from your website, portals, Instagram and WhatsApp, often in Spanish, and slow replies lose buyers. An automation that collects them in one place, detects the language, assigns an agent and starts a follow-up sequence usually pays for itself quickly and is easy to measure.

faqs.q: Can you automate work in tools we already use?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Most CRMs, accounting tools, booking systems and shared inboxes have APIs, and we connect them with off-the-shelf connectors or custom code. Where a tool has no API, we look for exports or other safe routes before suggesting a change of system.

faqs.q: Will AI automation replace our staff?
faqs.a: That is not how we design it. The aim is to remove copy-and-paste work and slow replies so your people spend their time on clients, deals and problems. Every flow has a person in charge of approvals and exceptions, and staff can see exactly what the system did and why.

faqs.q: Do your automations work in Spanish?
faqs.a: Yes. Customer-facing flows handle English, Spanish and mixed messages, which is how many Miami customers write. We test with real examples from your inbox before launch and set rules so anything sensitive or unclear goes to a person who speaks the customer's language.

faqs.q: How do you handle the time difference between London and Miami?
faqs.a: London is five hours ahead of Miami. We schedule live calls in your morning, when both teams are working, and use the hours before Miami wakes up to build and test. Changes go live outside your busiest hours, and your Signal Lead sends a written update so nothing waits on a call.

faqs.q: What happens if an automation breaks?
faqs.a: We set up alerts so failed runs are flagged to us and to the person who owns the process. Most issues come from a changed form, login or API, and we fix them as part of ongoing support. Nothing is left silently failing in the background.
